heading: Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Review
sample: Clinical synthesis of diagnosis and treatment
text: The study summarises the heterogeneity of autism, multidisciplinary assessment and the absence of a single biomarker with clinical diagnostic usefulness.
notProven: It does not replace local guidelines; a narrative review does not by itself quantify the effectiveness of each intervention.
linea: Broad clinical review. It does not replace local guidelines; a narrative review does not by itself quantify the effectiveness of each intervention.

heading: A systematic review of social camouflaging in autistic adults and youth: Implications and theory
sample: Studies of autistic adults and young people
text: The study identifies compensation, masking and assimilation strategies, with motivations including self-protection and social connection; the relationship with mental health appears complex and possibly bidirectional.
notProven: The literature does not show that masking by itself causes mental-health problems or that every autistic person masks.
linea: Systematic review. The literature does not show that masking by itself causes mental-health problems or that every autistic person masks.

heading: Interoception in individuals with autism spectrum disorder: a systematic literature review and meta-analysis
sample: 31 studies; meta-analysis of 5 comparable adult studies
text: The study did not find a uniform alteration in cardiac interoceptive accuracy in adults and found heterogeneous results in other dimensions.
notProven: It does not support the claim that autistic people universally have an 'interoceptive deficit'.
linea: Systematic review and meta-analysis with 31 studies; meta-analysis of 5 comparable adult studies. It does not support the claim that autistic people universally have an 'interoceptive deficit'.

heading: How auditory processing influences the autistic profile: A review
text: The study integrates differences in auditory processing and phenomena such as hyperacusis, misophonia and phonophobia, together with their relationships with overload, anxiety and sleep.
notProven: It is an integrative review and does not show that any specific auditory difficulty is present in every autistic person.
linea: Review. It is an integrative review and does not show that any specific auditory difficulty is present in every autistic person.

heading: Autism Spectrum Disorder and Sleep
sample: Paediatric literature on autism and sleep
text: The study reviews insomnia, assessment, co-occurring factors and behavioural and pharmacological options in autistic populations.
notProven: It does not turn every sleep problem into a 'symptom of autism'; specific causes still need to be assessed.
linea: Clinical review. It does not turn every sleep problem into a 'symptom of autism'; specific causes still need to be assessed.

heading: Melatonin for sleep disorders in people with autism: Systematic review and meta-analysis
text: The study found favourable effects on total sleep time, sleep latency and sleep efficiency compared with control/placebo.
notProven: Heterogeneity was very high and not every sleep parameter improved; this does not justify self-medication.
linea: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 15 studies. Heterogeneity was very high and not every sleep parameter improved; this does not justify self-medication.

heading: Pharmacological or non-pharmacological therapies? The impact of different therapies on sleep in children with autism spectrum disorder: A systematic review and network meta-analysis
text: The study compared melatonin, family sleep education, behavioural interventions, physical activity and complementary therapies; several showed signals of benefit.
notProven: Indirect rankings from a network meta-analysis depend on how comparable the studies are and are not equivalent to an individual recommendation.
linea: Systematic review and network meta-analysis of 35 randomised trials. Indirect rankings depend on study comparability and are not equivalent to an individual recommendation.

heading: A systematic review and meta-analysis of the relationship between sensory processing differences and internalising/externalising problems in autism
sample: Literature on sensory processing and mental-health/behavioural outcomes
text: The study supports associations between sensory-processing differences and internalising or externalising problems in autistic samples.
notProven: Associations do not prove causation, and sensory and psychological measures vary across studies.
linea: Systematic review and meta-analysis. Associations do not prove causation, and sensory and psychological measures vary across studies.

heading: Investigating alexithymia in autism: A systematic review and meta-analysis
sample: 15 articles comparing autistic and non-autistic groups
text: The study found higher rates and higher alexithymia scores in autistic groups.
notProven: It does not show that alexithymia is a core or universal feature of autism.
linea: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 15 articles comparing autistic and non-autistic groups. It does not show that alexithymia is a core or universal feature of autism.

heading: Pathological demand avoidance in children and adolescents: A systematic review
sample: Available literature on children and adolescents
text: The study concluded that PDA remained a controversial concept, with methodological problems and heterogeneity in how it was identified.
notProven: It does not validate PDA as an independent diagnosis or an established subtype of autism.
linea: Systematic review. It does not validate PDA as an independent diagnosis or an established subtype of autism.

heading: A Systematic Review of Pathological Demand Avoidance (PDA): A Veritable Diagnosis or a Case of Circular Logic?
sample: Studies of PDA measures and the PDA construct
text: The study re-evaluates the available evidence on PDA and the validity of tools used to identify it.
notProven: It should be labelled as methodological debate literature, not as confirmation of an official diagnosis.
linea: Systematic review. It should be labelled as methodological debate literature, not as confirmation of an official diagnosis.

heading: Verbal fluency and autism: Reframing current data through the lens of monotropism
text: The study shows substantial variability both between and within groups and proposes a neurodiversity-affirming reinterpretation through the lens of monotropism.
notProven: It is not a diagnostic validation of monotropism and does not show that monotropism explains every autistic attentional difference.
linea: Systematised narrative review of 17 verbal-fluency articles. It is not a diagnostic validation of monotropism and does not show that monotropism explains every autistic attentional difference.

heading: Who, when, where, and why: A systematic review of 'late diagnosis' in autism
text: The study shows that there is no uniform definition of 'late diagnosis': the age thresholds used in research vary greatly.
notProven: It does not support setting one universal age after which an autism diagnosis should be called late.
linea: Preregistered systematic review of 420 articles. It does not support setting one universal age after which an autism diagnosis should be called late.

heading: Systematic Review of Autism in Women: Invisibilised Profiles and Gender Bias
text: The study describes diagnostic delays, lower sensitivity of some tools for less externalising presentations, and the role of camouflaging and context.
notProven: It does not justify creating a 'female autism test' or assuming a single profile for autistic women.
linea: Systematic review of 26 studies (2015–2025). It does not justify creating a 'female autism test' or assuming a single profile for autistic women.

heading: What You Are Hiding Could Be Hurting You: Autistic Masking in Relation to Mental Health, Interpersonal Trauma, Authenticity, and Self-Esteem
text: The study found associations between masking and mental-health variables, interpersonal trauma, authenticity and self-esteem.
notProven: It is cross-sectional and does not establish the direction of causation.
linea: Cross-sectional study with 342 autistic adults. It is cross-sectional and does not establish the direction of causation.

heading: Suicidal Thoughts and Behaviors in People on the Autism Spectrum
sample: Literature on suicidal thoughts, attempts, risk/protective factors and assessment
text: The study summarises evidence on suicide risk in autistic populations and gaps in adapted assessment and intervention.
notProven: It cannot predict an individual's risk and does not replace urgent assessment when warning signs are present.
linea: Review. It cannot predict an individual's risk and does not replace urgent assessment when warning signs are present.

heading: Risk of Self-harm in Children and Adults With Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
text: The study found higher pooled odds for both self-harm and suicidality in autistic people compared with comparison groups.
notProven: Association sizes do not describe the risk of a particular person and do not by themselves explain the causes.
linea: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 31 studies. Association sizes do not describe the risk of a particular person and do not by themselves explain the causes.

heading: Anxiety and depression in adults with autism spectrum disorder: a systematic review and meta-analysis
text: The study found high rates of anxiety and depression, with estimates highly sensitive to assessment method and the presence of intellectual disability.
notProven: Methodological variability prevents applying one prevalence figure to the entire autistic population.
linea: Systematic review and meta-analysis. Methodological variability prevents applying one prevalence figure to the entire autistic population.

heading: Anxiety Levels in Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Meta-Analysis
text: Autistic children showed higher average anxiety levels than several comparison groups.
notProven: It does not mean that every autistic child has an anxiety disorder; the result is group-level and depends on the comparator.
linea: Meta-analysis of 83 articles. It does not mean that every autistic child has an anxiety disorder; the result is group-level and depends on the comparator.

heading: Assessment and Treatment of Anxiety in Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder in School Settings: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
text: The study reviews tools and interventions for anxiety in autistic pupils within school settings.
notProven: School-based evidence is more limited than clinical evidence and does not turn every form of school avoidance into anxiety.
linea: Systematic review and meta-analysis. School-based evidence is more limited than clinical evidence and does not turn every form of school avoidance into anxiety.
